title: Crispy Chicken Wings

items: 2 lb chicken wings, split into flats and drumettes, tips removed
1 Tbsp aluminum-free baking powder (not baking soda)
½ cup cayenne pepper hot sauce, such as Frank's RedHot
½ cup ranch or blue cheese dressing
2 medium carrots, peeled and cut into 3-inch sticks

steps: Pat the wings very dry with paper towels. Any moisture left on the skin keeps it from crisping.
In a large bowl, mix the baking powder, salt and garlic powder. Add the wings and toss until each one has a thin, even dusting.
Arrange the wings in the air fryer basket in a single layer, not touching. Most baskets fit about 1 lb, so cook in 2 batches if needed.

Air fry at 380°F for 20 min. Flip the wings, raise the heat to 400°F and cook 5–8 min more, until deep golden and crisp and the thickest drumette reads at least 165°F. Wings are juiciest at 175–185°F.
While the wings cook, whisk the melted butter and hot sauce together in a large bowl.
For buffalo wings, toss the hot wings in the sauce right before serving. Serve with the dressing, celery and carrots.
tips: Oven method: line a rimmed sheet pan with foil and set a wire rack on it. Spread the coated wings on the rack and bake at 425°F on the middle rack for 45–50 min, flipping halfway, until crisp and 165°F.
Use aluminum-free baking powder; regular can taste metallic. Never swap in baking soda, which tastes soapy.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Reheat in the air fryer at 375°F for 5–7 min, until hot (165°F) and crisp again. Sauced wings soften as they sit, so sauce only what you'll eat.
